summary: Yellowstone Regional Airport (COD/KCOD) serves Cody, Wyoming, serving as the primary air gateway to the east entrance of Yellowstone National Park, approximately 52 miles west of the town. The airport handles commercial and general aviation traffic, making it a convenient entry point for visitors heading to the Yellowstone ecosystem. Its location in the scenic Bighorn Basin region offers passengers immediate access to the rugged landscapes of northwestern Wyoming upon landing.
faqs:
Q: How far is Yellowstone Regional Airport from Yellowstone National Park?
A: The airport is roughly 52 miles east of the park's East Entrance, typically a one-hour drive to the boundary.

Q: What airlines serve Yellowstone Regional Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by regional carriers offering flights to and from Denver and Salt Lake City hubs, though service can vary seasonally.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates year-round, though flight frequencies may be reduced during the winter months.

Q: Can I rent a car at Yellowstone Regional Airport?
A: Yes, car rental agencies are available on-site, which is essential for reaching Yellowstone and other regional destinations.
transport_tips: Renting a car is strongly recommended as there is no public transit connecting the airport to Yellowstone National Park or surrounding destinations. Taxi services and shuttle options are limited and should be arranged in advance, especially during off-peak seasons. The airport is a short 8-mile drive east of downtown Cody, with straightforward access via US Highway 14/16/20.
local_tip: If you have time before or after your flight, visit the nearby Buffalo Bill Center of the West in downtown Cody—it's a Smithsonian-affiliated museum complex and one of the most comprehensive Western heritage museums in the country.
